title: Defects in a Batch
problem: Ten components independently have probability 0.3 of being defective. Find the mean and variance of the number of defective components.

hints.text: The count is binomial with n=10 and p=0.3.
For a binomial count, the mean is np and the variance is np(1-p).

solution.setup: Let X be the number of defective components, so X is Binomial(10,0.3).
solution.reasoning: The mean is np=10(0.3)=3. The variance is np(1-p)=10(0.3)(0.7)=2.1. Its standard deviation, if desired, is sqrt(2.1), approximately 1.449.
solution.sanityCheck: Three expected defects out of ten matches the 30% defect rate, and the variance is below the mean because failures and successes are both bounded per trial.

keyInsight: Independent Bernoulli contributions produce a binomial count with standard mean and variance formulas.
recognitionCues: A fixed number of independent yes/no trials with common success probability is binomial.
commonMistakes: Reporting np(1-p)=2.1 as the standard deviation rather than the variance.
followUps: How would positive dependence among defects affect the variance?
